cryptohome: Add new commandline features for cryptohome commandline tool. To add new data restore key, simply type: cryptohome --action=add_data_restore_key --user=your_user_name Then type in your password, wait for a few second, then the hex string of data restore key will be displayed if authenticated. To build authentication, testers can use switch "--restore_key_in_hex" to provide data restore key in HexString, for instance if testers type: cryptohome --action=check_key_ex --user=your_user_name --restore_key_in_hex=0123456789ABCDEF Cryptohome will use restore key in AuthorizationRequest and check if it can be authenticated. To mass remove keys, users need to provide exempt key labels. Every other keyset whose label is not in exempt_key_labels will be removed. For instance, if users have four keysets which are labeled as "l1", "l2", "l3" and "l4", say if they want to delete l1 and l2 and keep l3 and l4, they should type: cryptohome --action=mass_remove_keys --user=your_user_name --exempt_key_labels=l3,l4 After authenticated, l1 and l2 will be removed. BUG=chromium:945057 TEST=Flash image to physical device and use cryptohome command line to test. dlcservice: Unify into simple logic for exposed APIs Dlcservice exposes 3 main APIs: - Install - Uninstall - GetInstall Within this CL, we try and break those APIs into calling helpers for high level understanding that is simple. Sequence of events that should happen for each API: - Install: CreateDlc - Uninstall: UnmountDlc, DeleteDlc - GetInstall: Just return the installed DLC(s). Currently these APIs are dependent on the fact that |LoadDlcModuleImages()| will always fully succeed and give rise to a |installed_dlc_modules_| that is completely valid. |OnStatusUpdateAdvancedSignal()| will only return a single type of error as the user should not care whether |ImageLoader| was the reason for the failure, but the mounting itself failed. This will require improvements to |MountDlc()|. Note: No breakage of old unittests. BUG=none TEST=FEATURES="test" emerge-$BOARD dlcservice TEST=tast run $TEST_IP platform.DLCService Change-Id: I62e2e1b4df8b310fc08eb215e0874f94e21ed2fa Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1730169 Tested-by: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Jae Hoon Kim <kimjae@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org>

servo: micro + ccd on same instance (round 2). Note: This is a temporay hack as go/servoarch will provide the same functionality, however in this case we need this double feature earlier. Expect this to be gone with servoarch with the rest of postinit. This change adds a new layer to postinit to allow for servo micro and ccd on the same servo instance iff both micro and ccd are enumerated and on the same v4 hub. In that case, the servo micro is the main device, and all controls route to it. However, ccd backed controls are also available behind the ccd_cr50. prefix. This is off by default and can be enabled by having --allow-dual-v4 in the cmdline. To that effect the change adds that to the upstart script used in the lab.
